beats.narration: Priya has just started a new job at a Docklands fintech. Her adviser, Hannah Lewis, emails Caldova an application pack to open one super account and consolidate her old funds.
Priya's application pack heads across Melbourne to Caldova Client Operations on Flinders Lane.
Priya's application pack arrives at Caldova Client Operations.
The pack lands in the Onboarding inbox: a Caldova Super (Select) application in the Growth model, two rollovers, a $3,300 p.a. adviser fee consent and a BDBN naming Arjun.
Olivia's agent extracts every field from the pack and runs the NIGO checklist — ID verified electronically ✓, TFN supplied ✓, signatures ✓.
Olivia opens case REQ-20261103-DEMO01 for new member CS-2049817 and routes it for a KYC/AML screen, then to Benefits & Eligibility.
Felix runs KYC/AML screening on Priya — identity verified electronically, no PEP or sanctions match. All clear.
Ben checks the adviser fee consent, the beneficiary nomination and the product fit against the PDS, the trust deed and super law.
Ben: s99FA fee consent valid ✓, TMD fit ✓ — but the BDBN has only one witness, so it is treated as non-binding until Priya re-signs it in front of two adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries.

Rory lodges the SuperStream rollover from Harbourline Retail Super (about $41,800) now, and holds Southern Cross Industry Super (about $96,400) — rolling it over would end Priya's $520,000 Death & TPD cover.
Ivy confirms the Growth model (80/20) fits Priya's Growth risk profile and compares Growth, Balanced and Index Balanced on $138,200 — fees in dollars — in a client workbook.
Ben hands the case to Payments with the investment instructions.
Penny sets up the investment instructions: each rollover is invested in the Growth model on receipt, keeping 1% in the Caldova Cash Account for fees.
Cara sends Priya a welcome email and updates Hannah: re-sign the BDBN with two witnesses, and confirm or replace the insurance before the Southern Cross rollover.
